correctness.rationale: The Hsu--Qi--Brown server rule gives the exact recurrence \(x_{t+1}=(\beta+q^{K_t})x_t-\beta x_{t-1}\). For fixed \(K\), all three Jury inequalities are strictly positive under \(|q|<1\) and \(0\le\beta<1\). For the two-round product, two Jury inequalities are automatic and the third reduces exactly to \((\beta+q^{K_1})(\beta+q^{K_2})>-(1-\beta)^2\). The rational witness and direct recurrence replay agree with the symbolic result.

originality.rationale: The defining FedAvgM source studies server momentum empirically at fixed local epoch counts. The later dedicated server-momentum study treats system heterogeneity but changes the heterogeneous-computation update by normalizing client differences by local-step count and proves convergence only under a much smaller client-step condition. Focused searches found no published statement giving the exact raw-FedAvgM periodic-workload Schur criterion or the stable-frozen/unstable-switched witness.
residual_risks: Equivalent two-period matrix-product criteria may exist in older switched-control literature under different terminology.
The explicit instability uses a locally overshooting gradient step and does not apply to nonovershooting local steps.
The result does not classify arbitrary workload sequences or stochastic client sampling.

value.rationale: Server momentum was introduced to damp federated oscillations, while later work identifies time-varying local computation as an important systems effect. The result isolates a sharp opposite phenomenon: workload variation alone can destabilize server momentum even when every frozen workload and every local gradient map is stable. The exact criterion, the existence result for every positive momentum level, and the side-by-side stable FedAvg witness give a concrete robustness boundary rather than a routine fixed-quadratic calculation.
